problem: The visually hidden <thead class="tb-thead"> is meant to collapse to 1px below 40rem, but the rule `.tb-table thead { display:block; width:100% }` (specificity 0,1,1) beats `.tb-thead { width:1px }` (0,1,0). The absolutely positioned thead becomes full width and sticks out 21px past the right edge. clip-path hides it visually but it still counts as scrollable overflow. documentElement.scrollWidth goes from 390 to 411 (and 360 to 381) as soon as the user reaches the Warranty section. Mobile Chrome then widens the layout viewport, so the fixed bottom bar (Nazovi/WhatsApp/Viber/Procjena) drops 44–46px below the screen and only its top ~21px stays visible for the rest of the page. The page can also be panned sideways.
fix: In Warranty.astro, take thead out of the shared block rule: `.tb-table, .tb-table tbody { display:block; width:100% }`. Make the sr-only rule win: `.tb-table .tb-thead { position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip-path:inset(50%); white-space:nowrap }`, and in the ≥40rem block use `.tb-table .tb-thead { position:static; width:100%; height:auto; overflow:visible; clip-path:none }`. Add a safety net: `#jamstvo { overflow-x: clip; }`. I verified that injecting `.tb-table .tb-thead{width:1px}` keeps the bar at 675–740px at scrollY 12000.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-m360-barcut.png (bar cut to 21px). Measured: scrollWidth 411 at 390 and 381 at 360; bar top 719 / bottom 784 against innerHeight 740. With the fix, the bar stays at 675–740.

problem: At ≥1280 the sheet stretches to the height of the text column (xl:items-stretch), and that column is ~700px tall: eyebrow, 4-line H1, subline, 2 rows of CTAs, trust row. The sheet's bottom edge sits at 863px (1366×768) and 876px (1280×800). The payoff caption "Ovo nije crtež. Pravi krov · Zagreb →" (y 804–848 / 817–861), the title block and the trust row are all below the fold on the most common laptop sizes, so the animation's final beat lands off-screen.
fix: Size the hero to the viewport from lg up. (1) Reduce padding: `lg:py-14 xl:py-16` → `lg:py-10 xl:py-12`. (2) Cap the stage: `@media (min-width:64rem){ .hx-stage{ max-height: calc(100svh - 101px - 2.75rem - 4.5rem); } }` and at xl use `flex:0 0 auto; height: clamp(26rem, calc(100svh - 14rem), 42rem)` instead of stretching to the text column. The photo already uses object-fit:cover, and the drawing should use preserveAspectRatio xMidYMid meet. (3) Compress the text column on short screens: `@media (min-width:64rem) and (max-height:57rem){ .hx-display{font-size:clamp(2.75rem,4.3vw,4.75rem)} .hx-sub{margin-top:1rem} [data-hx-ctas]{margin-top:1.5rem} .hx-trust{margin-top:1.5rem} }`. Acceptance: the sheet's bottom edge (with caption) is ≤ innerHeight − 24px at 1280×720, 1366×768 and 1440×790.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-h1366.png, shots/rv-ad-h1280.png. Measured: sheet bottom 863 at 1366×768 and 876 at 1280×800.

page: / hero, animation 2.8–4.2 s and the finished frame
problem: The final beat doesn't read as intentional. (a) windowPoly (geometry.ts:235) is the whole house outline including the walls down to ground level (GY). The photo, a close-up of crijep-lim tiles, first appears inside the full house silhouette, so the walls turn into roof tiles (frame ~3.3 s) instead of the brief's "the roof shape becomes a window". (b) In the finished state the ghost drawing stays on top of the photo (INK_FINAL 0.34 and DIM_FINAL 0.5 in hero.ts:23-24; .hx-ink/.hx-dim at Hero.astro:598-605). Its side-elevation geometry doesn't line up with the photo's oblique view at all. The red 12 450 / 6 080 / 35° / RAL 7016 turn pink on blue-grey steel, and '6 080' and the RAL leader are cut off at the panel edges, so it looks like a compositing error. (c) The caption box (663–1112px) and the title block (1145–1360px) sit side by side on the bottom edge as two competing dark boxes.
fix: (a) Set windowPoly to the roof polygon only: points EL, A, A2/J0/B/B2 (ridge), WE2, ER2 and back along the eave, using the same target-edge mapping so it still opens to the full frame. Walls then stay drawn while the steel becomes photo. (b) Set INK_FINAL = 0 and DIM_FINAL = 0, and the CSS final state `.hx-ink,.hx-ruler,.hx-dash,.hx-dim{opacity:0}`. If you want to keep the drawing language on the photo, add one crisp annotation that registers with it instead: a 1px white leader to a snow guard labelled 'SNJEGOBRAN · RAL 7016'. (c) In the final state hide `.hx-tb` (opacity 0, 0.2 s) so the caption is the only overlay, or move the caption text into the title block's first row.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-cs-reveal.png (frames 3300–3900: tiles fill the walls), shots/rv-ad-zoom-final.png (pink ghost dimensions), shots/rv-ad-hf-4200.png

problem: The header phone link is `hidden xl:inline-flex` (Header.astro:55) and the mobile CTA bar is `lg:hidden`. From 1024 to 1279px the sticky header shows only the nav and the red CTA. Once the utility bar scrolls away, no phone number is visible anywhere, on touch tablets too, even though the brief says to judge the site by calls.
fix: Add a 44×44 icon-only tel button at lg: `<a href={telHref} class="kr-iconbtn hidden lg:inline-flex xl:hidden" aria-label="Nazovi 091 000 0000">` before the CTA, using the same style as the mobile phone button. Alternatively show the full number from lg by tightening the nav gap (gap-6 → gap-5) and the CTA padding (px-5 → px-4). Also consider showing MobileCtaBar under `@media (pointer:coarse) and (max-width:1366px)`.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-d1024-03.png (sticky header without phone), shots/rv-ad-h1024.png

problem: Section titles use a fixed lg:text-6xl (60px) inside 4/12 columns that are only 288px wide at 1024. 'Standard' renders 365px wide inside a 320px box: it overflows by 45px and ends 4px from the Warranty table border (table left at 369px), then breaks into 4 lines with an orphaned 'i'. 'Detalj / je / potpis.' leaves 'je' alone on a line. Two sections override the size locally (Managers #zgrade h2 clamp(…3.9vw…) = 40px; Faq .faq-head h2 clamp(…3.7vw…) = 38px), so at 1024 the H2s jump between 38, 40 and 60px from section to section.
fix: In SectionHead.astro replace `lg:text-6xl` with `lg:text-[clamp(2.625rem,4.1vw,3.75rem)]` (≈42px at 1024, 52px at 1280, 59px at 1440) and delete the local overrides (Managers.astro lines 123–127 and Faq.astro ~133–134). In Warranty.astro use `lg:col-span-5 xl:col-span-4` for the head and `lg:col-span-7 xl:col-span-8` for the table. Acceptance: no H2 scrollWidth > clientWidth, and no single-word lines at 1024/1100/1180.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-cs-1024orph.png. Measured at 1024: Warranty h2 glyph right edge 365 vs box 320 vs table left 369; zgrade h2 40px and pitanja h2 38px vs 60px elsewhere.

problem: Every [data-scan] has its own trigger at 'top 85%', so the 3–4 visible rail cards scan in lockstep: four red scan lines move at once alongside the red progress bar. That breaks rule 5, "only one red thing moves per screen". The scan also starts without waiting for the image. Measured: at +1000 ms the clip is fully open but img.complete is false and currentSrc is empty for cards 2–3. Visitors watch a red line uncover an empty antracit box, then the photo pops in with no animation (cards 2–3 were still grey at +3 s). Only card 1 is eager (Projects.astro:55).
fix: In reveal.ts: (1) before playing, await the image: `const img = el.querySelector('img'); const ready = img && !(img.complete && img.naturalWidth) ? Promise.race([img.decode().catch(()=>{}), new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1500))]) : Promise.resolve();` and play the timeline in onEnter after `ready`. (2) Sequence the scans: use `ScrollTrigger.batch('[data-scan]', { start:'top 85%', once:true, onEnter: els => els.forEach((el,i)=> gsap.delayedCall(i*0.22, ()=>play(el))) })` so lines cascade left to right, one at a time. In Projects.astro pass `eager={i < 3}` to ProjectCard, since the first three cards are in the first view of the section.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-scan-350s.png (4 cards clipped identically), shots/rv-ad-s-radovi-3000.png (cards 2–3 still empty at +3 s)

problem: The CTA cluster has no clear structure. The primary 'Besplatna procjena' (226px) sits alone and is narrower than the secondary row below it (Nazovi 232px + WhatsApp 149px = 393px), so the most important button looks smaller than the secondary group and the right edges step down unevenly. At 1024 all three stack with three different widths (226/232/149). Also at 1024 the sheet is vertically centred (`items-center`): its top at 289px doesn't line up with the eyebrow at 150px, so the panel floats in the middle of the column.
fix: Make the CTAs one block: on the data-hx-ctas wrapper (line 44) use `md:grid md:grid-cols-2 md:gap-3 md:max-w-[25rem]` instead of flex-col. Primary: `md:col-span-2 md:w-full` (h-14). Nazovi and WhatsApp each take 1fr (h-12), giving one clean 400px-wide block at every desktop size. On the hero grid (line 25) change `items-center` to `lg:items-start` and add `lg:mt-[3.25rem]` on the sheet wrapper so its top edge lines up with the H1 cap height. Alternatively stretch at lg as at xl.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-d1440-01.png, shots/rv-ad-h1024.png. Measured CTA boxes at 1440: [64,602,226×56], [64,670,232×44], [308,670,149×44]; at 1024 three rows.

problem: The page's display scale is inverted. At 1440 the H1 is 71.3px, while the FinalCta H2 is 72px (xl:text-[4.5rem]) and the WhatsApp band H2 is 68px. On mobile the H1 is 41.6px but the FinalCta H2 is 46px. The hero should carry the largest type on the page; at the moment the closing section shouts louder than the brand line.
fix: Fix the scale at H1 > billboard H2 > section H2. FinalCta.astro:37 → `text-[2.375rem] xs:text-[2.5rem] sm:text-[3.25rem] lg:text-[3.5rem] xl:text-[4rem]` (64px at 1440, 38px at 390). WhatsAppBand.astro:30 → `xl:text-[4rem]`. Section H2s stay at ≤60px (see the SectionHead clamp).
evidence: Measured via getComputedStyle: H1 71.28px; #procjena h2 72px; #slike h2 68px at 1440. At 390: H1 41.6px, #procjena h2 46px.

page: / hero photo (finished frame) and repeat visits / reduced motion
problem: Photo 17 ('zalazak') is centre-cropped to 5:4 at build time (`position="center"`, 1200×960). The crop removes the sunset sky and Zagreb roofline, which are the warm, human part of the shot. What's left is a flat field of tiles with a terracotta neighbour roof and a yellow façade wedged into the top-right corner. In the money shot of the hero this reads as a stock texture with a distraction in the corner, not 'Pravi krov · Zagreb'.
fix: Crop from the top so the golden-hour sky and skyline frame the anthracite roof: `position="top"` in the Picture (HeroSheet.astro) and `.hx-photo img { object-position: 50% 0% }` (Hero.astro). If the neighbour roof still dominates, try 'attention' cropping or `object-position: 35% 0%`. Lower the top stop of the .hx-photo::after scrim from 0.42 to 0.28 so the sky isn't muddied.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-hf-4200.png (current crop), src/assets/projects/krov-crijep-lim-zalazak.jpg (full frame with sky)

page: / hero animation (desktop full mode and mobile short mode)
problem: Two beats are mistimed. (1) After the hit the beam sits on the ridge for 0.26 s, then lifts over 0.34 s with power2.in (slow start), while strip laying starts 0.02 s after the lift. The hatched beam and its red Λ tip hang over the roof while the first strips and seam flashes play, so two focal points and two red things move at once (frames 1.3–1.5 s, mobile 1.0–1.4 s). (2) revealAt = stampAt + 0.3 and the stamp fades at revealAt + 0.1, so 'IZVEDENO', the payoff word, is readable for only ~0.4 s before the photo washes it pink.
fix: hero.ts:128 `liftAt = bendAt + 0.2`; line 136 `duration: 0.2, ease: 'power3.in'`; line 140 `layAt = Math.max(at(1.24), liftAt + 0.12)`; line 190 `revealAt = Math.max(at(2.84), stampAt + (short ? 0.5 : 0.7))`. Total length grows by ~0.35 s and stays inside the ~3.6–4 s budget.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-cs-p1.png and shots/rv-ad-cs-p2.png (beam still on the ridge at 1.5 s while strips lay), shots/rv-ad-cs-m3.png, shots/rv-ad-cs-reveal.png (stamp ghosted at 3.3 s)

problem: The callout labels (the section's content) are hidden under .motion and appear one by one: ring 0.2 s, then leader 0.55 s, then label 0.28 s, three times, and only after the scan finishes (whenScanDone). The right third of the section stays empty for ~4–5 s after the section enters view: at +1.5 s one leader is visible, at +3 s two of three. A normal scroll speed passes it by with an empty column, and the motion feels slow.
fix: Keep labels always visible: drop the `.motion .dsig-label` hide (~line 121) and animate leaders and rings only. Start at 'top 70%' and don't wait for the scan to finish: start when the scan is at ~60%, or use a fixed 0.5 s delay. Draw the three leaders with `stagger: 0.15, duration: 0.45`, so the whole set finishes in ≤1.2 s.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-cs-det.png (frames at +0.5/1.5/3/5 s), shots/rv-ad-detalj.png

problem: The left column (H2, phone, hours, WA/Viber, email and the 'Što se događa nakon slanja' list) ends ~310px below the form card at 1440 and ~400px below it at 1280: column bottoms 13853 vs form 13543. The bottom half of the right column is an empty grid-paper void next to the conversion form, and the form scrolls out of view while the visitor reads the steps.

(1) The Radovi rail progress is a solid 3px red bar ~400px long that moves (Projects.astro:70, bg-redline), the largest red element in the section and it competes with the CTA. (2) All six Services row numbers '01/06…06/06' are red (Services.astro:62), plus six red 'Procjena' links: 12 red marks in one section. (3) In FinalCta, the 'Što se događa nakon slanja' steps use red-outlined number boxes (line 96) next to the form's red active-step marker, red KORAK label and red phone icon.

(3) FinalCta.astro:96 `text-redline` → `text-linija`, box border `border-linija/30`. Keep red for the form's active step and the CTA buttons.

problem: The homepage reuses the same few photos, which makes the portfolio look thin. The hero photo (krov-crijep-lim-zalazak) is also the first Radovi card, right after 'Ovo nije crtež' → 'Ovo nije render.'. ravni-krov-trapez-atika-gromobran appears 3× (Services row 4, Radovi, Managers), and krov-crijep-lim-uvala-radnik appears 3× (Services, WhatsApp thumbnails, Radovi). Meanwhile atika-opsav-susjedni-krov, atika-opsav-kut-ljestve, atika-opsav-alat(-siroko) and falcani-krov-zid sit unused in src/assets/projects.

In Managers.astro:12/19 use atika-opsav-susjedni-krov.jpg (a multi-unit building context) instead of the gromobran shot. In the WhatsAppBand thumbnails use snjegobrani-odozgo / atika-opsav-kut-ljestve / falcani-krov-zid, so the 'three photos' are new images.

problem: A glossy iPhone mockup with a Dynamic Island, status bar and chat UI is the one SaaS-template element on the page. It breaks the drawing language every other section uses (hairlines, crop marks, mono annotations). On flat antracit, with equal-weight WhatsApp green and Viber purple blocks beside it, the band reads as a generic template block, and the thumbnails inside the phone are too small (78×100px) to show anything.

Optionally add one small chat bubble as an annotation ('Vidimo uvalu — dolazimo izmjeriti u četvrtak.'). Keep WhatsApp as the primary filled button and make Viber an outline button (border-viber text-white) so the two don't compete.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-s-slike-3000.png, shots/rv-ad-d1440-05.png

problem: The process photo carries a bar reading 'TIMELAPSE · TRI DANA U 15 SEKUNDI · USKORO' (lines 84–92). A 'coming soon' label on a premium homepage signals unfinished work, and unlike the other placeholders it isn't marked as a prototype example. The same photo also shows a worker kneeling at the roof edge with no visible fall protection, which is a poor trust signal next to 'pisano jamstvo'.
fix: Remove the overlay bar until the video exists: gate it with `const hasTimelapse = false` and render only the figcaption. Crop the worker out with `imgClass="object-[50%_70%]"` on the 4:5 frame, or swap in a harness shot from the shot list.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-d1440-09.png, shots/rv-ad-d1440-08.png

problem: On narrow screens the decorative aside (the house drawing plus the POSAO/MJESTO/KROV/FOTO list, ~150px) comes before 'Korak 01 · Što treba?' and the job chips. The first thing a mobile visitor sees in the form is a summary of empty fields, and the first tap target moves down by about a fifth of the screen.
fix: Below the 40rem container query, put the aside after the step content: `.rn-aside { order: 2 }` with `@container rn (min-width: 40rem) { .rn-aside { order: 0 } }`. Or collapse it on mobile into a single 24px mono progress row ('Posao — · Mjesto — · Krov — · Foto —') under the step tabs.

problem: Each service row uses `margin-inline:-1.25rem; padding-inline:1.25rem` (line 244) for the hover fill, so the row hairlines run from 44 to 1396px at 1440 (12 to 1012px at 1024). Every other section's rules (header lead, Managers list, FAQ, Warranty table) stop at the 64/1376px wrap edge, so this is the one section where the grid edge visibly breaks.
fix: Keep the bleed for the hover fill only. Set `.svc { margin-inline:0; padding-inline:0 }` and draw the hover background with `.svc::before { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0 -1.25rem; background:transparent; transition:background-color 200ms; z-index:-1 }`, with `.svc:hover::before { background: rgb(226 223 216 / .6) }`. Keep border-top and .svc-rule at the wrap width (`left:0; right:0`).
evidence: shots/rv-ad-d1440-03.png, shots/rv-ad-d1024-03.png

problem: The page has two horizontal rails with two different control layouts. Radovi has the counter '01 / 09' on the left, a red 3px progress bar and arrows on the right. Reviews has a black 2px progress bar on the left, the counter '01–03 / 04' between bar and arrows, and a different counter format. On one page this reads as two templates stitched together.
fix: Use one pattern for both rails: [counter 'NN–NN / NN', mono 11px, left] [1px track, 2px thumb in white/80 on dark or tinta on light, flex-1] [prev][next 44×44]. Extract it into a shared RailControls partial, or copy the identical markup and classes into both files.

problem: At tablet portrait the sheet stage is 16/10 (485px including the top bar, 47% of the screen; the brief says 42%). The primary 'Besplatna procjena' button starts at y=952 and the fixed bar at 959, so a 7px red sliver of the button peeks above the bar on first paint. It looks like a rendering glitch.

problem: The mono keyword line wraps inside a phrase ('LIMENI / KROVOVI, OPŠAVI I OLUCI') instead of at the red · separators. At 1366 the subline's second line starts with an em dash ('— krojeno i savijeno…').

problem: The same photos repeat on one page. The hero image, the 'Ovako izgleda gotovo.' gallery and the 'Već izvedeno.' project cards draw from overlapping sources, and galleryOf() only removes the hero image. Falcani krovovi has 2 photos and shows them 4 times: FalcIzlaz is both the hero and card 1, FalcZid is both Sl. 02 and card 2. On Opšav atike, 4 of the 5 project cards reuse the hero or gallery photos (Gromobran = hero; Medvednica, KutDetalj and Šljunak = Sl. 02–04). Dimnjaci has one photo, used as both the hero and the only card. Limeni krovovi (Zalazak = Sl. 02 + card), Popravak (UvalaRadnik = hero + card) and Oluci (SnjegobraniOdozgo = hero + card; SnjegobranCijev = gallery + card) do the same. When only one project is related, the 'Svi radovi' tile then spans 2 columns as a mostly empty bordered box.
fix: In [slug].astro, track a used set: `const used = new Set([service.image])`. Render related project cards first and add each p.image to used. Build the gallery as `[...service.gallery, ...related.flatMap(p => p.gallery)].filter(img => !used.has(img))`, deduplicated and limited to 4. If a related project's cover equals the hero, give it its next unused gallery image through a new optional `image` prop on ProjectCard. If that is not possible, fold that project into the 'Svi radovi' tile's legend instead of drawing a card. A cleaner option is to merge the two sections into one 'S gradilišta' section, where every photo tile is a project link with a mono caption. Add a rule that no ImageMetadata is rendered twice on one page. On dimnjaci (1 photo in total), hide the related grid and show only the 'Svi radovi' tile at full width.
evidence: shots/rv-ad-uf-dsheet-a.png, shots/rv-ad-uf-dsheet-b.png, shots/rv-ad-ua-dsheet-a.png, shots/rv-ad-ua-dsheet-b.png, shots/rv-ad-ul-d-04.png, shots/rv-ad-ud-dsheet-a.png

problem: The FAQ section on 5 of 6 service pages holds one question. Above it sits a 3-line display H2, 'Pitanja koja čujemo na svakom krovu.' (the Faq default title), next to a sticky 'Pitajte majstora' card. At 1440 that leaves about 300 px of empty papir under the single answer, and the section measures 747 px tall for one Q&A. The headline also promises questions 'on every roof' and then delivers one.
fix: Show at least 4 items, padding the service's own FAQ with relevant global items using the same pick() pattern as upravitelji-zgrada.astro: price per m², jamstvo, trajanje radova, je li procjena besplatna. For example: `const items = [...service.faq, ...pickGlobal(service.slug)].slice(0, 5)`. Pass a service-specific title such as `Pitanja o: ${service.title.toLowerCase()}.` (or a new per-service `faqTitle` field in site.ts). If fewer than 3 items remain, render a compact variant: one column, H2 at text-4xl, the ask card inline below, no sticky column, py-16.

page: every subpage (worst on /usluge/*, /radovi/*, /procjena, /kontakt, /upravitelji-zgrada, which have their own #procjena form)
problem: The primary CTAs are hard-coded to the homepage: Header.astro:61 `href="/#procjena"` and MobileCtaBar.astro:34 `href="/#procjena"`. On a service page that already has its own form, preselected with that service, tapping 'Besplatna procjena' in the header or 'Procjena' in the mobile bar leaves the page, loads the homepage and drops the preselection. On /procjena itself, the header CTA navigates away from the form. /radovi has no form, yet its hero CTA (ctaHref '/#procjena', line 48) and its bottom band button (line 132) also send visitors to the homepage form, even though a dedicated /procjena page exists. On /hvala, right after the visitor submits, the header still shows a red 'Besplatna procjena' button.
fix: Add a `formOnPage` boolean to Base (true wherever NalogSection or ProcjenaCta is rendered) and pass it to Header and MobileCtaBar. Use `href={formOnPage ? '#procjena' : '/procjena'}`, or detect it on the client: `if (document.getElementById('procjena')) a.href = '#procjena'`. On /radovi, change both CTAs to '/procjena'. On /hvala (hideMobileBar is already set), swap the header CTA for a WhatsApp 'Pošalji slike' button with the order number prefilled.

problem: The portfolio page titled 'Ovo nije render.' shows no photos in the first screen. The hero is 678 px tall at 1440 (896 px on mobile). problem: The last step has a required checkbox, "Pristajem da me Limarija Karamatić kontaktira u vezi upita." If it's left unticked, submit fails with "Potrebna je vaša privola…". Nađemo uzrok, a ne samo mrlju — uvale, sljeme, spojevi i dimnjaci."), "Limeni krovovi u Zagrebu", "Falcani krovovi u Zagrebu", "Opšav atike i ravni krovovi u Zagrebu", "Opšav dimnjaka u Zagrebu", "Oluci i snjegobrani u Zagrebu". problem: Service pages have no social proof near the form: no Google rating, no review, no years or warranty figure. They also have almost no objection handling. The FAQ shows only service.faq: one question on popravak, falcani, opšav atike, dimnjaci and oluci, and two on limeni krovovi. It sits under the generic heading "Pitanja koja čujemo na svakom krovu.", which looks broken with a single item. On an Ads click this is where people decide, and the homepage proof (ProofStrip, Reviews, Warranty) never reaches them.

(2) Between "Već izvedeno" and the FAQ, add a compact proof block: Google 4,9/5 with stars, one review card from `reviews`, and "10 god. pisano jamstvo" (all with ExampleTag until confirmed). Alternatively reuse <ProofStrip/> plus one Reviews card.

problem: The form doesn't deliver what the page promises. The section is titled "Pošaljite adresu zgrade.", the lead says "upišite adresu i kontakt", and the note says "Za ponudu trebamo: Adresu zgrade i ime upravitelja … OIB zgrade za R1 račun" and "Ponudu i fotografije šaljemo e-poštom". A building manager can't give what is asked, and the company can't e-mail the offer it promises. Separately, "R1 račun na zgradu" is the wrong term for a stambena zgrada. A building isn't a VAT payer, so what matters is a račun with the building's OIB. R1 matters to the izvođači and investitori the page also targets.

Step 3: add "Tvrtka upravitelja (nije obavezno)" and "E-pošta" (type=email, required in this variant), and optionally "OIB zgrade (ako ga imate)". In the copy, replace "R1 račun na zgradu" with "Račun na zgradu (OIB zgrade) · R1 za tvrtke".

problem: The form tag is `action="/hvala" method="get"` (lines 85–86). Without JS, the name, mobile number and location end up in the URL, browser history, server logs and analytics referrers. Photos are silently dropped, because GET can't upload files.

page: Homepage, "Dolazimo li do vas?" checker; WhatsApp prefills site-wide
problem: Typing "Sv. Nedelja" returns the fallback "Javite se — dogovorit ćemo izlazak.", because norm() expands "sv." only to "sveti", so "Sveta Nedelja" never matches. The match prefill builds "Pozdrav, trebam procjenu za krov u mjestu Trešnjevka.", but a kvart is not a mjesto, and "u mjestu Zagreb" is clumsy. Other prefills: the default "…za krov u " makes the user decline the place name, the service pages send "trebam procjenu (opšav i oblaganje dimnjaka) u ", and the FAQ sends "imam pitanje za krov:".
fix: In norm(), map `/\bsv(?:et[iao])?\.?\s+/g` to 'sv ' on both the query and the list. Make all prefills one pattern with no declension. ServiceArea.astro:865: `Pozdrav, trebam procjenu krova. Lokacija: ${hit.place}.` site.ts waHref default: 'Pozdrav, trebam procjenu krova. Lokacija: '. usluge/[slug].astro:289: `Pozdrav, trebam procjenu: ${service.title.toLowerCase()}. Lokacija: `. Faq.astro:74: 'Pozdrav, imam pitanje o krovu: '.

page: / (homepage, Warranty section #jamstvo affects the whole page)
viewport: every width below 640 px (measured at 360 and 390, both real-mobile emulation and reduced motion)
problem: The page is 21 px wider than the screen: scrollWidth 381 vs clientWidth 360, and 411 vs 390. The cause is the visually hidden table header `.tb-thead`. It is meant to be 1×1 px with position:absolute, but the rule `.tb-table, .tb-table tbody, .tb-table thead { display:block; width:100% }` has higher specificity (0,1,1 vs 0,1,0), so it gets width:100% of the viewport. With no positioned ancestor it sits at left:21 px, so its right edge lands at 381. On real phones the layout viewport stretches to 381 px: the page can be panned sideways and the fixed mobile CTA bar becomes 381 px wide, so the red 'Procjena' cell is cut by 21 px. Before the table's reveal finishes, the reveal transform on `.tb` hides the bug. After the reveal, and always with no JS or reduced motion, the page overflows. The spec says no horizontal scroll anywhere.
fix: In the Warranty.astro <style>, add `position: relative;` to `.tb` and give the hidden header higher specificity: `.tb-table .tb-thead { position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip-path:inset(50%); white-space:nowrap; }`. Keep the `@media (width >= 40rem)` reset as `.tb-table .tb-thead { position:static; width:auto; height:auto; … }`. Alternatively, drop `thead` from the shared `display:block; width:100%` selector. Then check that document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth at 360 and 390.
evidence: Overflow script: `/` at 360 → sw 381 / iw 381 / ih 784 instead of 740 (viewport stretched). Offenders: thead.tb-thead right=381, MobileCtaBar ul right=381. Every other route at 360–1440 has 0 overflow. Screenshots: shots/rv-qa-360-home-reduce.png, shots/rv-qa-360-bar-crop.png.

viewport: ≥1024 px for the late LCP; all viewports for reduced motion, Save-Data, low-memory phones and repeat visits in the same session
problem: The hero photo is the largest element on screen, but it is marked `loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low"` (HeroSheet.astro lines 48–50). On top of that, hero.ts hides it with `gsap.set(photo, { autoAlpha: 0 })` (line 97) and only reveals it at about 2.8 s (lines 192–211). In real Chrome the H1 paints at about 0.12 s, then the photo becomes the new LCP when it appears: 3104 ms at 1440, 3052 ms at 1280, 3076 ms at 1024, all unthrottled. With 4× CPU and slow 4G it is 5932 ms. So every first desktop visit has a field LCP over 2.5 s ('needs improvement'), and no network speedup can fix it. Lighthouse desktop shows 99 and LCP 0.9 s only because its trace ends before the reveal, so the lab score hides the problem. A second case: when motion is off (reduced motion, Save-Data, deviceMemory ≤ 2, or a repeat visit with hx-played), the photo is visible from the first frame but is still fetched lazily at low priority. LCP is then the photo at 4208 ms (390 px, throttled) and 3276 ms (1440, throttled), against 0.8 s for the text.
fix: (1) Paint the photo from the first frame and hide it with a cover instead of opacity. Chrome's LCP ignores elements with opacity 0 but does not account for one element covering another. Keep `.hx-photo` at opacity 1, add an opaque `.hx-cover` div above it (background grafit-2 plus the grid, under the drawing) and animate the cover away. For the 'window' effect, put the clip on the cover with a hole: `clip-path: path(evenodd, 'M0 0H{w}V{h}H0Z M{house polygon}')`, built from windowPolys(), then tween it to empty. Do not use `autoAlpha` on the photo. (2) In HeroSheet.astro set `loading="eager"`, `fetchpriority="high"` and `decoding="async"`. (3) In Base.astro add an optional `preloadImage` prop and, on / only, emit `<link rel="preload" as="image" type="image/avif" imagesrcset="…480w,…720w,…960w,…1200w" imagesizes="(min-width: 1440px) 760px, (min-width: 1024px) 52vw, calc(100vw - 2.5rem)" fetchpriority="high">`, using getImage() with the same widths. Expected result: LCP at about the image paint time (under 1.5 s on 4G) in every motion mode. Add a RUM or web-vitals check, because lab Lighthouse cannot catch this.
evidence: PerformanceObserver(LCP) on the production build, scratchpad/qa/lcp.mjs and lcp2.mjs: 1440 → '72ms SPAN → 116ms SPAN(133k) → 3104ms IMG(185k)'. Reduced motion at 390 → IMG at 4208 ms (load 4182 ms). Lighthouse desktop: perf 99, LCP 0.9 s on the H1 (trace too short).

problem: Lighthouse mobile on the production build: / scores 74 (FCP 3.3 s, LCP 5.1 s on the H1 with about 900 ms render delay, SI 3.5 s, TBT 0, CLS 0); /usluge/popravak-krova scores 80 (FCP 2.9 s, LCP 4.4 s). The causes: (a) 7 render-blocking stylesheets on / and 5 on service pages (ExampleTag.css 13 KB gzipped plus 2–3.5 KB component chunks), which Lighthouse estimates cost 1,650 ms and 1,510 ms. (b) No font preload. Archivo latin (88 KB) and latin-ext (85 KB) are both needed for Croatian characters, yet they are discovered only after the CSS loads. The H1 repaints wider when Archivo swaps in, which pushes LCP later and causes desktop font-swap CLS of 0.011–0.034 in the page heroes. Plex Mono adds 4 more files (56 KB). (c) The only eager image on the homepage is the first project card in the section-5 rail (`eager={i === 0}`, Projects.astro line 55). It is far below the fold, yet it is fetched at Medium priority at 45 ms (103 KB), alongside the fonts. The homepage's initial transfer is 1,049 KiB (images 664, fonts 229, JS 80, CSS 28, HTML 47), against the creative direction's first-load budget of 700 KB.
fix: (1) astro.config.mjs: `build: { inlineStylesheets: 'always' }`. That is about 28 KB gzipped inlined per page and removes every render-blocking request. (2) Base.astro: preload the two Archivo woff2 files: `import archivoLatin from '@fontsource-variable/archivo/files/archivo-latin-wdth-normal.woff2?url'` (and the latin-ext file) → `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" href={archivoLatin} crossorigin>`. Better still, self-host one subset file (Basic Latin + ČĆĐŠŽčćđšž + „“–—·²° with the wght and wdth axes kept, via pyftsubset) at about 50 KB instead of 173 KB, and preload only that. Drop the Plex Mono 500 weight (use 400 with font-weight synthesis off) or subset it the same way. Add a metric-matched fallback (`@font-face { font-family:'Archivo Fallback'; src:local('Arial'); size-adjust:…; ascent-override:… }`, or Astro's Fonts API, which generates one) to remove the swap reflow. (3) Projects.astro line 55: remove `eager={i === 0}` so the rail cards are all lazy. Target: mobile FCP under 2 s, LCP under 2.5 s, initial transfer under 700 KB.
evidence: scratchpad/qa/lh_.json and lh_usluge_popravak-krova.json (Lighthouse 13.5, mobile). Render-blocking list: RadniNalog.css, ServiceArea.css, Warranty.css, MobileCtaBar.css, Hero.css, ExampleTag.css, WhatsAppBand.css. problem: The red scan line on photos is moved by tweening the CSS `top` property, from 0% to 100% (reveal.ts lines 64–67). Every frame moves a laid-out, absolutely positioned element, so each photo reveal logs layout shifts. Chrome attributes them to SPAN.scanline. CLS (session window) measured while scrolling the production build: /radovi 0.157 at 390 (above the 0.1 'good' limit, and 3× the creative-direction target of ≤0.05); / 0.069 at 390; /usluge/popravak-krova 0.032; /o-nama 0.028. Lighthouse also flags it above the fold on /usluge/popravak-krova (CLS 0.019, PageHero `.ph-photo > span.scanline`).
fix: In reveal.ts, animate a transform instead of `top`: `gsap.set(line, { top: 0, opacity: 1, y: 0 }); tl.to(line, { y: () => el.offsetHeight, duration: 0.9, ease: 'draft' }, 0)`, keeping the clip-path tween on `el` (clip-path does not shift layout). In global.css add `will-change: transform;` to `[data-scan] > .scanline`. Remove the `top:'100%'` tween. The local `:has(> .scanline[style*='top: 100%'])` workarounds key on that inline style, so they need updating or (since they are slated for removal anyway) deleting. Expected CLS from scans: 0.
evidence: scratchpad/qa/cls.mjs on the production build: '/radovi 390 CLS=0.1566 (0.1221 SPAN.scanline, 0.0854 SPAN.scanline×2)', '/ 390 CLS=0.0690'. Lighthouse layout-shifts on popravak-krova: scanline score 0.012 + 0.0048 + 0.0007.

problem: When the rail reaches the end, the script sets `next.disabled = true` (Projects.astro lines 182–183; Reviews.astro lines 257–258) while that button still has focus. A disabled button drops focus, so focus falls to <body> and a keyboard user loses their place. Measured: after 6 presses of 'Sljedeći radovi' activeElement is BODY. On Recenzije at 1440 a single press of 'Sljedeće recenzije' does the same, since 4 cards with 3 visible means one step reaches the end. The next Tab then jumps to an unrelated card further down.
fix: Keep the buttons focusable. Replace `btn.disabled = x` with `btn.setAttribute('aria-disabled', String(x))`, return early in the click handler when `aria-disabled==='true'`, and move the existing `disabled:` Tailwind styles to `aria-disabled:opacity-30 aria-disabled:cursor-default`. Or, before disabling, `if (document.activeElement === next && atEnd) prev?.focus()`. Apply the same to the prev button at the start.

problem: In the production build, canonical and og:url carry a trailing slash (`https://www.limarija-karamatic.hr/usluge/popravak-krova/`), because `new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)` gets the directory-format pathname. Every internal link, the Service.url, BreadcrumbList and ItemList URLs and the nav all use the no-slash form (`/usluge/popravak-krova`). Both /radovi and /radovi/ return 200. Canonical, links and structured data therefore point at different URLs. The dev server shows no slash, so this is only visible in the build. 404.html gets `canonical https://…/404/`.
fix: astro.config.mjs: `trailingSlash: 'never'` (optionally `build: { format: 'file' }`) so URLs match how links are written. Base.astro line 29: `const path = Astro.url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '') || '/'; const canonical = new URL(path, Astro.site);`. Skip the canonical tag when `noindex` is true (404, /hvala). Configure the host (Cloudflare Pages) to 301 the slash variant to the no-slash one.
evidence: Production dist: usluge/popravak-krova/index.html canonical '…/usluge/popravak-krova/' vs Service.url '…/usluge/popravak-krova' and BreadcrumbList item '…/usluge/popravak-krova'. 404.html canonical '…/404/'. curl 127.0.0.1:4400/radovi/ → 200.

problem: Each homepage service card's quote link is `/?usluga=${slug}#procjena` (Services.astro line 85). The query string differs from the current URL, so clicking it on the homepage triggers a full reload of the homepage (about 1 MB plus a re-render) just to preselect step 1 of a form that is already on the page. On mobile that means a white flash and a delayed jump, on the spec's 'service cards open the form preselected' path.

'smooth' : 'auto' })` and focus the step-1 heading (`[data-rn-heading]`). A small exported helper in src/lib/form.ts (`preselectJob(slug)`) avoids duplicating the resolveJob logic.

problem: The form is `action="/hvala" method="get"` (lines 85–86). Without JS, submitting puts the visitor's name, mobile number, location and notes into the URL query (/hvala?ime=…&mobitel=…). That ends up in browser history, server and CDN logs, analytics and Referer headers, which is a privacy and GDPR problem for a site that 'could ship'. A GET request also cannot carry the up to 6 photos the step-2 file input collects.
fix: Point the form at the planned Cloudflare Pages Function: `action="/api/nalog" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"`, and have the function answer with `303 See Other` to `/hvala?nalog=KR-1234`. The JS path in form.ts already has the fetch('/api/nalog', POST) stub. Until the backend exists, leave a TODO and note in the prototype handover that no-JS submission is demo-only.
evidence: No-JS run (scratchpad/qa/nojs.mjs): all 3 steps visible, submit enabled, so submission would GET /hvala with the field values. Source: RadniNalog.astro lines 85–86, form.ts line 4.
